why.1 Nephi 20–21: Nephi's Isaiah block. Set it beside Isaiah 48-49 and the King James wording is the same.
why.2 Nephi 7–8: Jacob's block. It matches Isaiah 50-51, chapters most scholars date to the exile, long after Lehi left.
why.2 Nephi 12–24: The long block: thirteen chapters of Isaiah in a row, in King James English.
why.2 Nephi 27: Reworks Isaiah 29 into a prophecy about a sealed book. The clearest case of Isaiah being reshaped.
why.Mosiah 14: Abinadi quotes Isaiah 53 whole. His sermon rests on it, so this block is hard to wave off.
why.3 Nephi 22: The risen Jesus gives the Nephites Isaiah 54, again in King James wording.
why.Isaiah 48–49: The King James text behind 1 Nephi 20-21. This is the side-by-side that starts the argument.
why.Isaiah 50–51: The King James text behind 2 Nephi 7-8.
why.Isaiah 2–14: The thirteen chapters copied at 2 Nephi 12-24. Skousen found the wording tracks later King James printings.
why.Isaiah 29: The chapter 2 Nephi 27 rewrites. Its sealed-book language becomes a prophecy of the gold plates.
why.Isaiah 53: The source for Mosiah 14. Christians read it as the suffering servant, and the wording carries over whole.
why.Isaiah 54: The source for 3 Nephi 22 — 'Sing, O barren' and all that follows.

why.2 Nephi 12:16: Helps their side. It adds 'the ships of the sea,' wording apologists say matches the Greek against the King James.
why.2 Nephi 16:2: Cited for the double plural 'seraphims' in the early printings. That is English form, not Hebrew.
why.2 Nephi 19:1: The clearest sample. It drops the King James italic 'her,' leaving the verb with nothing to act on.
why.2 Nephi 12–24 (variant pattern): The whole Isaiah block, cited as the data set. Wright counted the changes across it and found the clustering.
why.Isaiah 2:16: The King James verse for comparison. It has two 'and upon all' clauses. 2 Nephi 12:16 has three.
why.Isaiah 6:2: The King James verse with 'seraphims.' The double plural is the translators' English.
why.Isaiah 9:1: The King James verse that italicises 'her.' Dropping that one word is what breaks the sense in 2 Nephi 19:1.

why.2 Nephi 14:5: Has 'shall be a defence' where the Hebrew word chuppah means canopy. The King James error, carried over.
why.2 Nephi 16:2: Cited for keeping the King James plural 'seraphims' in the early printings. Hebrew already makes the word plural.
why.2 Nephi 21:3: Repeats 'make him of quick understanding,' which misses the Hebrew line about delight in the fear of the LORD.
why.Mosiah 14: Abinadi's whole sermon is Isaiah 53 in King James English. The longest stretch showing the pattern.
why.Isaiah 4:5: The King James source. It reads 'upon all the glory shall be a defence' — the rendering at issue.
why.Isaiah 11:3: The King James source of 'make him of quick understanding,' the phrase the Book of Mormon keeps.
why.Isaiah 6:2: The King James verse with 'seraphims.' A 1611 English plural, not a feature of the Hebrew.
why.Isaiah 53: The chapter behind Mosiah 14. Compare the two and the King James wording runs straight through.

why.1 Nephi 20–21: Nephi quotes Isaiah 48-49. Most scholars date those chapters to the exile, well after Lehi left Jerusalem.
why.2 Nephi 7–8: Jacob quotes Isaiah 50-51, also from the disputed second half of Isaiah.
why.2 Nephi 9:50–51: Quotes Isaiah 55:1-2, 'come ye to the waters,' from the same exile-dated section.
why.Mosiah 14: Abinadi builds a whole sermon on Isaiah 53. The costliest case for the answer that blames translation.
why.3 Nephi 20:32–45: Jesus quotes Isaiah 52 to the Nephites, including 'they shall see eye to eye.'
why.3 Nephi 22: Jesus gives them Isaiah 54. It sits in the same late block of chapters.
why.Isaiah 48–49: The chapters behind 1 Nephi 20-21. Isaiah 48 treats the exile in Babylon as already under way.
why.Isaiah 50–52: The source of 2 Nephi 7-8 and of part of 3 Nephi 20.
why.Isaiah 53: The servant chapter. It is the source of Mosiah 14, which is why this case bites so hard.
why.Isaiah 54: The source of 3 Nephi 22, from the same block of chapters.
why.Isaiah 55:1–2: The source of 2 Nephi 9:50-51. Compare them: 'come ye to the waters,' almost word for word.

why.3 Nephi 12–14: The Nephite Sermon on the Mount. Near-identical to Matthew 5-7 in King James English.
why.3 Nephi 13:13: The doxology: 'For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory.' Missing from the earliest copies of Matthew.
why.3 Nephi 13:4,6,18: Three verses ending 'reward thee openly.' That last word is a later addition in Matthew's manuscripts.
why.3 Nephi 12:27: Reads 'it is written by them of old time' where Matthew has 'ye have heard.' Welch cites this as a real change.
why.3 Nephi 12:44: Keeps 'bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you' — clauses the earliest copies of Matthew lack.
why.Matthew 5–7: The King James Sermon on the Mount, which 3 Nephi 12-14 follows almost word for word.
why.Matthew 6:13: The King James verse with the doxology. Modern Bibles drop it or footnote it.
why.Matthew 6:4,6,18: The King James verses with 'openly.' The word is absent from the earliest Greek copies.
why.Matthew 5:27: 'Ye have heard that it was said' — the King James wording 3 Nephi 12:27 changes.
why.Matthew 5:44: The King James verse with the extra clauses. Set it beside 3 Nephi 12:44 and they match.

why.2 Nephi 4:17: Nephi says 'O wretched man that I am' — Paul's line in Romans, spoken around 590 BC.
why.2 Nephi 9:39: 'To be carnally-minded is death.' That is Romans 8:6, in a sermon dated centuries before Paul.
why.1 Nephi 22:20: Quotes Moses in Peter's wording from Acts 3, not in the wording of Deuteronomy itself.
why.Alma 5:52: 'The ax is laid at the root of the tree' — John the Baptist's line, about a century early.
why.Moroni 7:45–47: Reads like 1 Corinthians 13, almost word for word. Same phrases, same order: 'suffereth long,' 'never faileth.'
why.Moroni 10:8–17: Tracks Paul's list of spiritual gifts in 1 Corinthians 12, down to the phrase 'the same Spirit.'
why.Romans 7:24: Paul's cry, which Nephi uses first. Paul wrote it about 650 years later.
why.Romans 8:6: Paul's contrast of the carnal and spiritual mind, which 2 Nephi 9:39 reproduces.
why.Acts 3:22–23: Peter's version of Deuteronomy 18. The clause 'in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you' is Peter's, and Nephi has it.
why.Matthew 3:10: John the Baptist's axe-at-the-root saying, which Alma 5:52 uses long before he said it.
why.1 Corinthians 13:4–8: Paul's charity passage. Set it beside Moroni 7:45-47 and the phrases run in the same order.
why.1 Corinthians 12:4–11: Paul's gifts passage, matched clause for clause by Moroni 10:8-17.

why.Alma 12:9–37: The first half of the sermon, on hardened hearts and entering God's 'rest.' That is the Hebrews 3-4 argument.
why.Alma 13:1–20: The priesthood section, 'after the order of the Son,' following the shape of Hebrews 5 and 7.
why.Alma 13:17–19: The Melchizedek summary: king of Salem, prince of peace, none greater. The tightest match with Hebrews.
why.Hebrews 3:7–4:11: Where 'my rest' is argued out at length. Alma 12 uses the same idea in the same order.
why.Hebrews 5:6–10: 'A priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec' — the phrase behind Alma's 'order of the Son.'
why.Hebrews 7:1–4: The passage Alma 13:17-19 tracks. Scholars call it the author's own build from Genesis 14 and Psalm 110.
why.Psalm 110:4: One of the two Old Testament sources the Hebrews author fused. Alone, it says only 'a priest for ever.'
why.Genesis 14:18–20: The other source. These three verses are all the Old Testament says about Melchizedek — which is Wright's point.

why.Mormon 9:22–24: The Nephite commission. Read it beside Mark: devils, new tongues, serpents, deadly drink, the sick recovering.
why.Ether 4:18: The shorter echo — 'he that believeth and is baptized shall be saved.' Same disputed passage, used twice.
why.Mark 16:15–18: The long ending of Mark. Absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus, and judged a later addition by most scholars.

why.1 Nephi 18:25: The arrival list — 'the cow and the ox, and the ass and the horse' found waiting in the promised land.
why.Enos 1:21: Nephite herds, 'and also many horses.' Not one stray mention. The claim recurs.
why.Alma 18:9–12: The hardest verse for the tapir answer. Ammon prepares the king's 'horses and chariots' — an animal in harness.
why.3 Nephi 3:22: Whole populations moving with 'their horses, and their chariots.' Horses at scale, not as a curiosity.
why.Ether 9:19: Adds elephants, and two names left as 'cureloms and cumoms.' The blank record covers the elephants too.

why.1 Nephi 4:9: Laban's sword of 'most precious steel.' This is the Old World half, and the Vered Jericho find answers it.
why.1 Nephi 16:18: Nephi's bow 'made of fine steel,' broken in Arabia. Old World again, so concede it plainly.
why.2 Nephi 5:15: The New World half. Nephi teaches his people to work in iron and steel, in America.
why.Jarom 1:8: An industry, not a relic. Iron, copper, brass and steel worked into tools and weapons of war.
why.Ether 7:9: Jaredite swords 'molten out of the hill.' That is smelting, which is what the archaeology does not find.

why.Mosiah 9:9: The seed list: 'corn, and of wheat, and of barley,' plus neas and sheum. Wheat is the unanswered one.
why.Alma 11:7,15: Partly helps them. Barley runs the Nephite weights, and little barley was in fact farmed in ancient North America.
why.Alma 1:29: Nephites with 'abundance of silk and fine-twined linen.' This is the silk half of the claim.
why.Ether 9:17: Jaredite 'silks' and fine linen. The wild-silk answer has to stretch back this far too.
why.Ether 10:24: Jaredites weaving 'silks, and fine-twined linen.' The second silk text, so one answer must cover both peoples.

why.3 Nephi 1:1: Names Lachoneus as chief judge. The name looks like Greek for 'the Laconian,' a Spartan.
why.3 Nephi 19:4: The list of twelve disciples. Timothy and Jonas are Greek names, in a list of Nephite ones.
why.3 Nephi 9:18: The risen Jesus says 'I am Alpha and Omega' — Greek letters, to a people with no Greek.
why.Revelation 1:8: Where the phrase comes from. The wording matches, which is the point: John's Greek in a Nephite mouth.

why.1 Nephi 4:26: 'The brethren of the church' in Jerusalem, 600 BC. The weakest of the three. Any translator needs some word here.
why.2 Nephi 26:26: 'Out of the synagogues,' long before there were any. Also weak. This is likely just the translator's word.
why.Alma 16:13: Synagogues 'built after the manner of the Jews.' Harder than bare vocabulary, but still arguable.
why.Alma 21:4–6: Synagogues built by a rival sect. Here the word names a real institution, not just a loose label.
why.2 Nephi 29:3–10: The strong one. Nephi answers 'A Bible! A Bible! We have got a Bible' — an argument of the 1820s.

why.Introduction ('the fulness of the everla: The book's own claim to hold the fulness of the gospel. That claim is what Galatians is being used to test.
why.1 Nephi 13:34–40: Their frame: plain and precious parts were 'kept back,' so a further book was needed.
why.3 Nephi 27:13–21: Cuts against you. Jesus here defines the gospel as the cross, repentance, baptism and enduring — which sounds familiar.
why.Galatians 1:6–9: The verse that works. Paul puts himself and an angel alike under the test of the gospel already given.
why.Revelation 22:18–19: Does not prove what people think. The warning is about 'this book,' meaning Revelation, not the whole Bible.
why.Deuteronomy 4:2: Shows why that argument fails. The same warning sits here, and nobody thinks it closed the Old Testament.
why.Jude 3: 'The faith which was once delivered unto the saints.' Cited for a closed canon, but it is about teaching, not a book list.
why.Hebrews 1:1–2: God 'hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son.' Used to argue the last word has been given.

why.2 Nephi 25:23: The verse the case turns on: 'it is by grace that we are saved, after all we can do.'
why.Moroni 10:32–33: The harder verse. Deny yourselves of all ungodliness, and 'then is his grace sufficient.' No idiom removes that.
why.Alma 11:37: Amulek says God 'cannot save them in their sins.' Read as a limit on grace, though Christians say much the same.
why.Ephesians 2:8–9: The reply text: saved by grace through faith, 'not of works, lest any man should boast.'
why.Romans 11:6: Paul's either/or. If by grace, 'then is it no more of works.' The two do not blend.
why.Romans 4:4–5: Wages against gift. God 'justifieth the ungodly,' which is the opposite of paying for a finished effort.
why.Titus 3:5: 'Not by works of righteousness which we have done' — saved by mercy instead.
why.Galatians 2:21: The stake. If righteousness comes by law, 'then Christ is dead in vain.'

why.2 Nephi 5:21–23: The verse the case rests on. A 'skin of blackness' comes 'because of their iniquity,' so they would not be 'enticing.'
why.Alma 3:6–9: Ties dark skin to a 'mark' set on the fathers. It puts the same curse on anyone who marries in.
why.3 Nephi 2:14–15: The reverse. 'Their curse was taken from them, and their skin became white.' Curse and colour move together.
why.Jacob 3:8–9: Cuts partly against you. Jacob rebukes Nephite racism, and says Lamanite skins may be whiter at the judgment.
why.2 Nephi 30:6 (1830/1981 variants): The 1981 edit. 'White and delightsome' became 'pure and delightsome.' The church changed the wording itself.
why.Mormon 5:15: 'A dark, a filthy, and a loathsome people.' The same link runs to the end of the book.
why.Acts 17:26: God 'hath made of one blood all nations.' The clearest biblical answer to a curse marked on skin.
why.Acts 10:34–35: Peter says God 'is no respecter of persons,' and accepts people in every nation.
why.1 Samuel 16:7: God 'looketh on the heart,' not the outward appearance. The exact opposite of skin as a mark.
why.Galatians 3:28: 'Neither Jew nor Greek… ye are all one in Christ Jesus.' The gospel erases the line this curse draws.
why.John 7:24: 'Judge not according to the appearance.' Short, and it lands right on this.
why.Revelation 7:9: The end of the story. Every nation and tongue stands before the throne, all in white robes.

why.2 Nephi 2:22–25: The core text. Without the fall they 'would have had no children,' and 'Adam fell that men might be.'
why.Alma 12:22–26: Alma takes the same line. The fall made this life a 'probationary state,' so it had to happen.
why.Genesis 1:28: The verse that does the work. 'Be fruitful, and multiply' is spoken before the fall, not after.
why.Genesis 2:17: The command Adam broke. It frames the fall as disobedience, with death as the penalty.
why.Romans 5:12–19: Paul's account. Sin and death entered by one man, and judgment came 'to condemnation.' Not a happy event.
why.Romans 8:20–22: Creation 'made subject to vanity,' and groaning. The fall as damage, not as a needed step.
why.1 Timothy 2:14: Paul calls the fall a transgression, brought on by deception. Nothing here treats it as a blessing.
why.1 Corinthians 15:21–22: 'By man came death.' Paul makes the fall the problem Christ answers, not part of the plan.

why.Moroni 8:8–23: The passage at issue. Infant baptism is 'solemn mockery before God,' and those who teach it 'must go down to hell.'
why.Mosiah 3:16–21: The same doctrine, put gently. Children are covered by 'the blood of Christ,' not by baptism.
why.2 Nephi 2:25: 'Adam fell that men might be.' Supplies the frame in which children are born innocent, not guilty.
why.Psalm 51:5: 'In sin did my mother conceive me.' The usual proof-text. It is a psalm of confession, not a doctrine of infant guilt.
why.Ephesians 2:3: 'By nature the children of wrath.' The strongest of the inherited-nature verses.
why.Romans 5:12, 18–19: Condemnation came 'by one man's disobedience.' The verse the whole original-sin case leans on.
why.Genesis 8:21: 'The imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth.' Note 'from his youth' — not from conception.
why.Psalm 58:3: 'The wicked are estranged from the womb.' Poetry about the wicked, not a claim about every baby.
why.1 Corinthians 15:22: 'As in Adam all die.' Cited for inherited death, which their side grants, so it settles little.

why.Mosiah 15:1–5: Abinadi says Christ is 'the Father and the Son… one God.' As tight a unity as anything in the Bible.
why.Mosiah 16:15: Calls Christ 'the very Eternal Father.' Apologists use it too, to show the wording is not a slip.
why.Alma 11:26–29, 38–39: The plainest exchange in the book. Zeezrom asks 'Is there more than one God?' Amulek answers 'No.'
why.2 Nephi 31:21: Ends 'which is one God, without end.' It ties the one-God claim to the way of salvation.
why.Mormon 7:7: Father, Son and Holy Ghost 'are one God.' The same formula near the close of the book.
why.3 Nephi 11:27: Jesus gives the baptism words: 'the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Ghost are one.'
why.Testimony of Three Witnesses ('one God'): Printed at the front of every copy. It gives praise to Father, Son and Holy Ghost, 'which is one God.'
why.Deuteronomy 6:4: 'The LORD our God is one LORD.' Israel's basic confession, and the standard being applied here.
why.Isaiah 43:10: 'Before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.' It rules out gods who became gods.
why.Isaiah 44:6–8: 'Beside me there is no God… I know not any.' The flattest denial of many gods in the Bible.
why.John 10:30: 'I and my Father are one.' Cited because 3 Nephi 11:27 says the same thing in the same words.
why.1 Timothy 2:5: 'There is one God, and one mediator.' New Testament monotheism, as plain as Alma 11.

why.1 Nephi 11:18 (1830 vs 1837): The 1830 text called Mary 'the mother of God.' In 1837 she became mother of the Son of God.
why.1 Nephi 11:21 (1830 vs 1837): 1830 read 'the Lamb of God, yea, even the Eternal Father.' The 1837 edition inserts 'the Son of.'
why.1 Nephi 11:32 (1830 vs 1837): 1830 had 'the everlasting God, was judged of the world.' The same three words were added here.
why.1 Nephi 13:40 (1830 vs 1837): 1830 read 'the Lamb of God is the Eternal Father.' The fourth and last of the four edits.
why.John 1:1, 14: Cuts against the easy version of this argument. The Word 'was God' and became flesh, so the 1830 wording was not strange.
why.Colossians 2:9: 'In him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.' More reason the first edition read as normal Christianity.
why.Isaiah 9:6: Calls the child 'The mighty God, The everlasting Father.' The Bible does the very thing the 1830 text did.
why.Titus 2:13: 'The great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ.' Another place the Bible calls Jesus God outright.

why.Jacob 2:24–30: The core text. David's and Solomon's wives were 'abominable,' and no man may 'have save it be one wife.'
why.Jacob 3:5: Repeats the rule as a standing command. One wife, no concubines. Jacob adds that the Lamanites kept it better.
why.Mosiah 11:2: King Noah's many wives mark him out as wicked. The book uses the practice as a sign of a bad king.
why.Ether 10:5: Riplakish, the same pattern among the Jaredites. Two peoples, one verdict on the practice.
why.Deuteronomy 17:17: The law given to kings: 'Neither shall he multiply wives to himself.' The Bible agrees with Jacob here.
why.1 Kings 11:1–11: Solomon's wives 'turned away his heart,' and God takes the kingdom from him. D&C 132 lists him among those who sinned not.
why.Matthew 19:4–6: Jesus goes back to the start: 'they twain shall be one flesh.' Two, not more.
why.1 Timothy 3:2: A church leader must be 'the husband of one wife.'
why.Genesis 2:24: The pattern set before any law. A man and 'his wife,' one flesh.

why.Moroni 8:18: The verse it turns on. God is 'unchangeable from all eternity to all eternity,' in their own scripture.
why.Mormon 9:9–11, 19: God 'the same yesterday, today, and forever.' Mormon argues that a God who changed would 'cease to be God.'
why.Moroni 7:22: God 'being from everlasting to everlasting.' A third witness in the book to the same idea.
why.3 Nephi 24:6: 'I am the Lord, I change not.' Jesus gives the Nephites the line from Malachi.
why.Psalm 90:2: 'From everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.' The Bible uses the same formula Moroni 8:18 uses.
why.Malachi 3:6: 'I am the LORD, I change not.' The source of the line quoted at 3 Nephi 24:6.
why.Isaiah 43:10: The sharpest one. 'Before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.' That is about being, not mood.
why.Isaiah 44:6: 'I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God.'
why.James 1:17: 'No variableness, neither shadow of turning.' Mormon 9:9 uses that phrase almost word for word.
why.Numbers 23:19: 'God is not a man.' Blunt, and the plainest reply to a God who was once a man.

why.Alma 34:32–35: The passage. 'This life is the time for men to prepare to meet God,' then comes 'the night of darkness.'
why.2 Nephi 9:38: 'Wo unto all those who die in their sins… and remain in their sins.' No second chance in view.
why.Mosiah 2:36–39: Ends in 'a never-ending torment' for the man who dies an enemy to God. The same two outcomes.
why.Mosiah 26:25–27: At the last trump, those who 'never knew me' are sent away. No spirit-world preaching appears here.
why.Hebrews 9:27: 'Appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.' The Bible agreeing with Alma.
why.Luke 16:26: The 'great gulf fixed' after death. Nobody crosses it in either direction.
why.2 Corinthians 6:2: 'Now is the day of salvation.' The urgency is for now, not later.
why.John 8:24: 'Ye shall die in your sins' if you do not believe. Death set as the deadline.

why.Alma 7:10: The verse. Read the exact words: 'at Jerusalem which is the land of our forefathers.' Land, not city.
why.Micah 5:2: The Bethlehem prophecy. It is what Alma 7:10 is accused of getting wrong.
why.Matthew 2:1–6: The fulfilment, with the priests quoting Micah. Bethlehem is five miles from Jerusalem.
why.Luke 2:4–7: The birth in Bethlehem. It does not settle the case, since a 'land of Jerusalem' could take it in.

why.1 Nephi 13:26–29, 34, 40: The charge itself. A 'great and abominable church' took 'many parts which are plain and most precious' from the Bible.
why.1 Nephi 14:20–26: Says the apostle John's book was 'plain and pure' when it left him. So the loss must come after.
why.Isaiah 40:8: 'The word of our God shall stand for ever.' The promise a wholesale gutting would break.
why.Matthew 24:35: Jesus says 'my words shall not pass away.' The same promise, from him.
why.1 Peter 1:24–25: 'The word of the Lord endureth for ever,' applied by Peter to the gospel that was preached.

why.Mormon 6:10–15: The final battle. Ten thousand at a time, and no burial ground has ever been found.
why.Ether 15:2: 'Nearly two millions' of Jaredites slain. That scale is what makes an empty record surprising.
why.Alma 2:19: Exact figures — 12,532 and 6,562 dead in one day. The text is precise, which invites a test.
why.Helaman 3:7–11: Cities and temples 'of cement,' plus shipping. These are concrete claims about building, not vague ones.
why.Mosiah 11:8–10: King Noah's palace and temple, in gold, silver, iron, brass and copper. A named material culture.
why.2 Nephi 5:15–16: A temple built 'after the manner of the temple of Solomon,' plus iron and steel work.

why.Mormon 9:32–34: The 'reformed Egyptian' verse. It also holds their best answer: the script was 'altered by us,' so no outsider knows it.
why.1 Nephi 1:2: The starting claim. A record in 'the learning of the Jews and the language of the Egyptians.'
why.Omni 1:20–22: A stone with engravings, brought to a king and read. Writing on stone, not just on plates.
why.Mosiah 8:11–13: Plates found in the ground with rusted swords, and nobody able to read them.
why.Jacob 4:1–3: Helps their side. Jacob says writing on anything but plates 'must perish,' which is why nothing else would survive.

why.Title Page: Says the book is written to the Lamanites, 'a remnant of the house of Israel.' The identity claim at issue.
why.1 Nephi 13:30: Promises the Gentiles will not 'utterly destroy the mixture of thy seed.' Lehi's line lives on here.
why.2 Nephi 30:4–6: The remnant will learn 'that they are descendants of the Jews.' A direct claim about American peoples.
why.Alma 10:3: Traces Lehi to Manasseh, son of Joseph. The book's own family line, which the DNA question tests.
why.Helaman 15:11–13: Prophesies the Lamanites brought back 'in the latter times.' Missionary work to Native Americans was built on this.
why.3 Nephi 21:2–7: Jesus ties the last days to 'a remnant of the house of Jacob' in this land. The same claim, from him.

why.1 Nephi 18:23: The landing. A party of roughly twenty to thirty people, and the clock starts here.
why.2 Nephi 5:6–16: The split, naming who went with Nephi. Then a temple and metal work, inside one generation.
why.Jarom 1:8: 'We multiplied exceedingly,' says Jarom. Buildings, tools and a full set of weapons, only a few generations in.
why.Alma 2:19: The precise figure: 12,532 Amlicites and 6,562 Nephites dead in a day, about 500 years after the landing.
why.Alma 28:2: 'Tens of thousands of the Lamanites were slain' in one battle. Armies on a national scale.
why.Mormon 6:10–15: Cumorah. Ten thousand under each commander, and about 230,000 Nephite dead.
why.Ether 15:2: 'Nearly two millions' of Jaredites already slain. The largest number the book gives.

why.Mosiah 8:13–18: The book's own picture of a seer: a man who 'can look' into interpreters and translate. It describes its own method.
why.Mosiah 28:11–16: Mosiah translates 'by the means of those two stones which were fastened into the two rims of a bow.'
why.Ether 3:23–28: Where the two stones come from. God gives them so the sealed writing can be read later.

why.Words of Mormon 1:3–7: Mormon says he added the small plates 'for a wise purpose' he does not know. The replacement text, flagged in advance.
why.1 Nephi 9:2–6: Nephi is told to make a second set of plates 'for a wise purpose in him, which purpose I know not.'
why.1 Nephi 19:1–6: Supports their side. The second record is set up early in the book, not improvised in 1828.

why.Testimony of Three Witnesses: The statement at the front of every copy. An angel and a voice — the visionary half of the evidence.
why.Testimony of Eight Witnesses: The other statement, and the stronger one for them. Plain daylight handling, with no angel in it.
why.Ether 5:2–4: The book predicts its own witnesses: 'unto three shall they be shown by the power of God.'
why.2 Nephi 27:12–13: The same promise again. Three witnesses, and no one else shall view it. The plan was in the text first.
why.Deuteronomy 19:15: 'At the mouth of two or three witnesses.' The biblical rule the whole arrangement copies.
why.2 Corinthians 13:1: Paul repeating that rule. Together these show the format was chosen, not stumbled into.

why.Testimony of Eight Witnesses: The only claim of ordinary handling of the plates. It is also the nearest thing to an examination that ever happened.

why.Alma 46:12–13: The title of liberty. Offered as a match for the battle scenes in The Late War, and one of the weaker parallels.
why.3 Nephi 24–25: Malachi given to the Nephites. It turns up in the parallel lists, but the King James cases cover it better.
why.Ether 1–15 (structure): The Jaredite story, cited for its shape. A people crossing water, a buried record, a nation wiped out.
why.Ezekiel 37:15–20: The two sticks, Judah and Joseph. The Bible verse both Ethan Smith and Latter-day Saints build on.
why.Isaiah 18: 'A nation scattered and peeled.' Ethan Smith read that as America — the sort of reading in the air then.

why.Genesis 11–12: The Bible's own Abraham story. The Book of Abraham adds material not found here, which is what needs a source.
why.Abraham 1:1–3 (Pearl of Great Price): The opening of the published text. These English words were said to come from a papyrus we can now read.

why.2 Nephi 3:6–18: The same prophecy inside the Book of Mormon. 'A choice seer will I raise up out of the fruit of thy loins.'
why.2 Nephi 4:1–2: Nephi says Joseph's prophecies 'are written upon the plates of brass.' The claimed source for the missing Genesis text.
why.Genesis 50:22–26 (KJV): How Genesis really ends. Joseph dies, and no seer is foretold. Read it and the addition stands out.
why.JST Genesis 50:24–38: The added verses themselves. About fourteen of them, and no ancient copy of Genesis has any.

why.2 Nephi 5:10: The Nephites keep the law 'in all things.' That phrase is what makes the priesthood problem sharp.
why.2 Nephi 5:26: Nephi consecrates Jacob and Joseph as 'priests and teachers.' A man of Joseph's tribe appointing priests.
why.2 Nephi 25:24: 'We keep the law of Moses,' said again later in the book. So it is not a passing remark.
why.1 Nephi 5:9: They 'offer sacrifice and burnt offerings.' Sacrifice, which the law hands to Aaron's line alone.
why.Mosiah 2:3: Burnt offerings 'according to the law of Moses,' centuries later. The practice keeps going.
why.Jacob 1:18: Jacob's own words. He and Joseph were 'consecrated priests… by the hand of Nephi.'
why.Alma 10:3: The family line that creates the problem. Lehi comes from Manasseh, not from Levi.
why.Numbers 3:9-12: The Levites given to Aaron, and 'the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.'
why.Numbers 16:39-40: After Korah, no one 'which is not of the seed of Aaron' may offer incense. The rule, with a warning attached.
why.Deuteronomy 33:8-11: Levi's blessing. It gives him the incense and the 'whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar.'
why.Hebrews 7:13-14: The plainest verse. Of another tribe, 'no man gave attendance at the altar.'
why.2 Chronicles 26:16-21: King Uzziah burns incense and is struck with leprosy. What happened when a non-priest tried it.

why.2 Nephi 5:16: Nephi's temple, built 'after the manner of the temple of Solomon.' The first, and the boldest claim.
why.Alma 16:13: Temples in the plural, beside synagogues. It is no longer one building.
why.Alma 26:29: Missionaries entering 'their temples' in Lamanite lands. Temples spread across the map.
why.Helaman 3:9: Cities with 'their temples, and their synagogues, and their sanctuaries.' Building them is routine by now.
why.Helaman 3:14: 'Their building of temples' listed among ordinary Nephite doings. The plural is settled by then.
why.Deuteronomy 12:5-14: The one-place law. Offer only 'in the place which the LORD shall choose,' not 'in every place that thou seest.'
why.1 Kings 8:29: Solomon's prayer, which fixes that place at the Jerusalem temple.
why.2 Kings 23:4-20: Josiah tearing down the rival altars, just before Lehi left. It shows how hard the rule was pressed.

why.3 Nephi 11:8-17: The descent itself. 'Behold, I am Jesus Christ.' The heart of the book, and what this argument aims at.
why.3 Nephi 26:13: He taught them 'for the space of three days,' then came often. The length is what troubles people.
why.Acts 3:20-21: The verse the argument uses. It does not prove what people think, since Jesus did appear after this.
why.Acts 1:9-11: The ascension, and the promise that he will come back the same way. It rules out nothing in between.

why.D&C 84:2-5: The prophecy. A temple 'shall be reared in this generation,' and 'this generation shall not all pass away' first.
why.D&C 114:1: David Patten sent on a mission 'next spring.' He was killed months before the spring came.
why.D&C 124:49-51: Their answer, inside their own canon. When enemies stop a commanded work, God 'requires that work no more.'
why.Deuteronomy 18:20-22: The test being applied. If the thing 'follow not, nor come to pass,' the LORD did not speak it.
why.Ezekiel 33:33: Fulfilment as the mark of a true prophet. Weaker than Deuteronomy 18, so do not lead with it.
why.Jeremiah 28:9: The same test, but narrowed to prophecies of peace. Note that limit before you quote it.

why.D&C 89:1-9: The revelation itself. Verse 2 says it is sent 'not by commandment or constraint' — the line this case turns on.
why.Mark 7:18-19: Jesus says what enters a man 'cannot defile him.' The verse behind the claim that food rules were set aside.
why.Colossians 2:16-23: 'Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink,' and 'touch not; taste not; handle not.' The closest fit.
why.1 Timothy 4:1-5: Warns that 'commanding to abstain from meats' marks a falling away. Strong wording, though it names food, not drink.
why.Romans 14:14-17: 'The kingdom of God is not meat and drink.' Paul makes it a matter of conscience, not of standing.
why.Matthew 11:19: Jesus was called 'a winebibber' by his critics. Cited because he drank wine, which D&C 89 counsels against.

why.Numbers 15:38-39: The fringes, worn so 'ye may look upon it, and remember.' The church cites the same purpose, so this helps their case.
why.Deuteronomy 22:12: The fringe command again. Note that it is outer clothing, given to Israel under the law of Moses.
why.Colossians 2:16-23: Warns against measuring Christian standing by outward keeping. The question is the checkpoint, not the cloth.
why.Matthew 23:5: Jesus on those who 'make broad their phylacteries.' That is about display, so it fits private clothing badly.
why.1 Samuel 16:7: God 'looketh on the heart,' not the outward appearance. The general rule being appealed to.

why.D&C 132:19-20: The core text. 'Then shall they be gods, because they have no end… because they have all power.'
why.D&C 132:37: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob 'are not angels but are gods.' Named men, said to be there already.
why.Abraham 3:22-26: The council before this life, and 'we will go down… and we will make an earth.' Where the creating role comes from.
why.Isaiah 43:10: The verse to press. 'Before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.'
why.Isaiah 44:6-8: 'Is there a God beside me? yea, there is no God; I know not any.' God saying he knows of no others.
why.Isaiah 45:5: 'There is none else, there is no God beside me.' The same denial a third time, which is why all three are quoted.
why.Genesis 3:5: The serpent's offer: 'ye shall be as gods.' The first promise of godhood in the Bible, and who made it.
why.Psalm 90:2: 'From everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.' There was no time when God was not God.

why.Official Declaration 2: The 1978 announcement that ended the ban. It is printed in their own scripture, so the history is not deniable.
why.Acts 10:34-35: 'God is no respecter of persons.' The verse to ask about, and the one their own Acts parallel rests on.
why.Galatians 3:28: 'Ye are all one in Christ Jesus.' No ethnic line is left standing inside the church.
why.Acts 17:26: God 'hath made of one blood all nations.' One human family, from one origin.
why.Colossians 3:11: 'Christ is all, and in all,' with the ethnic labels listed and then cancelled.
why.Revelation 7:9: Every nation and tongue before the throne. The end the ban could not be fitted into.

why.John 18:20: Jesus says 'in secret have I said nothing.' The verse to set beside a covenant of non-disclosure.
why.Matthew 10:26-27: 'What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light.' The gospel as public by design.
why.Ephesians 5:11-13: Fits badly. Paul is writing about shameful deeds done in secret, not about reverent ritual.

why.Abraham 3:22-26: The spirits 'organized before the world was.' The teaching of spirit children starts here.
why.D&C 93:29: 'Man was also in the beginning with God.' The pre-mortal life the Mother doctrine is built on.
why.D&C 132:19-20: Eternal marriage brings 'a continuation of the seeds forever.' That is where the idea of divine parents is set out.
why.Deuteronomy 6:4: 'The LORD our God is one LORD.' Israel's confession, with no second divine parent in it.
why.Isaiah 44:6-8: 'Beside me there is no God.' God saying he knows of no other, which is the point pressed here.
why.Jeremiah 7:18: The only 'queen of heaven' in the Bible. Cakes baked for her provoke God to anger.
why.Jeremiah 44:17-25: The longer passage on that same cult, and the judgment on it. This is the title's one biblical use.
why.John 4:24: 'God is a Spirit.' Used against the idea of divine parents producing spirit offspring.

why.D&C 93:21: 'I was in the beginning with the Father, and am the Firstborn.' Their own text for Christ's origin.
why.Moses 1:33: 'By the Son I created them.' Part of their strong answer, since it makes Christ the Creator.
why.Abraham 3:24: 'We will take of these materials, and we will make an earth.' Creation as shaping matter already there.
why.John 1:1-3: The verse to press. 'Without him was not any thing made that was made' puts Christ outside the made things.
why.Colossians 1:16-17: 'He is before all things,' and 'by him were all things created.' It answers the firstborn point in the next breath.
why.Micah 5:2: His 'goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.' No starting point for him.
why.Hebrews 13:8: 'Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.' No rise from one state to another.
why.John 8:58: 'Before Abraham was, I am.' Jesus taking God's own name for himself.

why.Moses 4:1-4: Satan's offer: 'here am I, send me, I will be thy son.' Where the shared-parentage picture comes from.
why.Abraham 3:27-28: Two answer the call, and 'I will send the first.' The rival-plan scene, in their canon.
why.D&C 76:25-27: 'An angel of God who was in authority… he was Lucifer.' Their own text on what Satan was.
why.Colossians 1:16: The key verse. 'Thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers' is Satan's class, and Christ made them.
why.Ezekiel 28:13-15: 'Thou wast created,' said twice. Read of Satan, it puts him among creatures.
why.John 1:3: 'Without him was not any thing made that was made.' No spirit sibling escapes that scope.
why.Hebrews 1:4-6: The Son 'made so much better than the angels,' who are told to worship him. A difference in kind, not rank.
why.Nehemiah 9:6: God made 'the heaven of heavens, with all their host,' and that host worships him. Angels as creatures.

why.D&C 130:22: The canon text. 'The Father has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's.'
why.D&C 131:7-8: 'There is no such thing as immaterial matter.' Even spirit is matter, which is the frame behind all this.
why.Abraham 3:22-24: Creation as organising 'these materials.' God works with matter that was already there.
why.Abraham 4:1: 'They, that is the Gods, organized and formed the heavens and the earth.' Gods in the plural, in their scripture.
why.John 4:24: 'God is a Spirit.' The usual reply, though their answer to it has some force.
why.Numbers 23:19: 'God is not a man.' Short, and aimed straight at the King Follett teaching.
why.Hosea 11:9: 'I am God, and not man.' The same statement, from a second prophet.
why.Psalm 90:2: 'From everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.' There was no time when he was not God.
why.Isaiah 43:10: 'Before me there was no God formed.' It rules out a God who was made, or who rose.
why.Isaiah 45:5: 'There is none else, there is no God beside me.' The plural Gods of Abraham 4:1 run into this.
why.Malachi 3:6: 'I am the LORD, I change not.' A God who was once a man has changed a great deal.
why.Hebrews 11:3: The worlds 'framed by the word of God,' not from things that appear. Against shaping eternal matter.

why.2 Corinthians 11:3-4: 'Another Jesus, whom we have not preached.' The phrase this whole argument borrows.
why.Galatians 1:6-9: The matching warning about 'another gospel.' Paul puts himself under the same test.
why.Matthew 24:23-24: 'False Christs, and false prophets.' Too blunt for this case, and it will land as an insult.
why.1 John 4:1-3: The test John gives is whether a spirit confesses 'Jesus Christ is come in the flesh.' Latter-day Saints pass that test.

why.Abraham 3:22-23: The intelligences 'organized before the world was.' The text this doctrine is built on.
why.D&C 93:29: 'Man was also in the beginning with God.' Intelligence 'was not created or made,' which is the sharp part.
why.Moses 3:5: God created all things 'spiritually, before they were naturally.' A spirit creation, ahead of the physical one.
why.1 Corinthians 15:46-47: Do not lean on this. Their answer is right that Paul is talking about resurrection bodies.
why.Zechariah 12:1: The LORD 'formeth the spirit of man within him.' The spirit made in the person, not before.
why.Genesis 2:7: Man 'became a living soul' when God breathed into formed dust. The soul starts here, not earlier.
why.Isaiah 44:24: God 'formed thee from the womb.' The forming is dated to the womb, not to a prior life.

why.D&C 130:22: Father and Son with bodies, the Holy Ghost 'a personage of Spirit.' Three beings, stated in canon.
why.Abraham 4:1: 'They, that is the Gods, organized and formed the heavens and the earth.' Creation by more than one.
why.Alma 11:28-29: Their own book cuts against them here. 'Is there more than one God?' 'No.'
why.2 Nephi 31:21: Father, Son and Holy Ghost, 'which is one God, without end.' The Book of Mormon on the Bible's side.
why.Deuteronomy 6:4: 'The LORD our God is one LORD.' The confession the rest of these verses rest on.
why.Isaiah 44:24: The sharpest one. God stretches the heavens 'alone' and spreads the earth 'by myself.' No council.
why.Isaiah 43:10: 'Before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.' None before, and none after.
why.Isaiah 45:5-6: 'There is none beside me. I am the LORD, and there is none else.' Said twice in two verses.
why.1 Corinthians 8:4-6: 'There is none other God but one.' Note that verse 5 grants 'gods many' as titles, which their side quotes.
why.John 17:20-23: Their strongest verse, not yours. Believers are to be one 'even as we are one,' which reads relationally.
why.John 10:30: 'I and my Father are one.' It will not settle this, since both sides read it their own way.

why.D&C 42:18,79: Helps their side. Their own canon sends killers to 'the laws of the land,' not to ritual death.
why.Mosiah 3:11: 'His blood atoneth for the sins' of the fallen. Their own scripture on how far the atonement reaches.
why.Hebrews 10:12-14: 'By one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.' One offering, with nothing to add.
why.1 John 1:7: The blood of Jesus 'cleanseth us from all sin.' All of them, with no class held back.
why.John 19:30: 'It is finished.' Three words, and they carry this case.
why.Hebrews 9:26: Christ appeared 'once… to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.' Once, not again and again.
why.Isaiah 53:5-6: 'The LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.' The whole load put on one person.
why.1 Timothy 2:5-6: 'One mediator,' who 'gave himself a ransom for all.' No second payment from the sinner.

why.Jacob 2:24: 'David and Solomon truly had many wives… which thing was abominable before me.' Their own book, against the practice.
why.Jacob 2:27-28: The command itself. One wife, no concubines, because God delights 'in the chastity of women.'
why.Jacob 2:30: Their escape clause. 'If I will… raise up seed unto me, I will command my people.' The whole defence rests here.
why.1 Timothy 3:2: A church leader must be 'the husband of one wife.' Applied here to the man leading the church.
why.Matthew 19:4-6: Jesus on marriage: 'they twain shall be one flesh.' Two people, joined by God.
why.Genesis 2:24: The pattern Jesus was quoting. One man, one wife, one flesh.

why.Jacob 2:27: One wife and no concubines, in their own scripture. The rule these sealings sit against.
why.Romans 7:2-3: A wife 'is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth.' The verse this case turns on.
why.Mark 10:11-12: Jesus on remarrying while a spouse lives. Note that it is about divorce, so it fits sealings only loosely.
why.Exodus 20:14: 'Thou shalt not commit adultery.' Blunt, and unproved here. The DNA testing cuts the other way.

why.D&C 132:52-54: The verses themselves. Emma must 'receive all those that have been given' to Joseph, or 'she shall be destroyed.'
why.D&C 132:64: The same warning widened to any first wife who refuses. So it is not a one-off about one marriage.
why.Ephesians 5:25: 'Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church.' Read it beside verse 54, then stop.
why.1 Peter 3:7: Husband and wife as 'heirs together of the grace of life.' Equal standing, not a condition placed on her.
why.Colossians 3:19: 'Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them.' Short, and it lands.

why.John 8:44: The devil as 'a liar, and the father of it.' Far too heavy here. Using it will end the conversation.
why.Ephesians 4:25: 'Speak every man truth with his neighbour.' The standard being applied to the 1844 sermon.
why.Proverbs 12:22: 'Lying lips are abomination to the LORD.' The plainest measure of a technically true denial.
why.Colossians 3:9: 'Lie not one to another.' Third in a row making the same point, so one of these would do.

why.D&C 132:61-63: The plural-marriage law, never taken out of their canon. It is why this is still a live question.
why.Matthew 22:30: 'In the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage.' It cuts against eternal marriage itself.
why.1 Timothy 3:2: 'The husband of one wife,' said of leaders. That is exactly whose second sealings are at issue.

why.Exodus 20:13: 'Thou shalt not kill.' The simplest measure of what happened at Mountain Meadows.
why.Matthew 5:44: 'Love your enemies.' These people were not even enemies. They had already surrendered.
why.Romans 12:19: 'Vengeance is mine; I will repay.' Aimed at the revenge feeling behind the killings.

why.1 Peter 2:23: Christ 'reviled not again' and 'threatened not.' The contrast being drawn with the pistol at Carthage.
why.Matthew 26:52: 'All they that take the sword shall perish with the sword.' Jesus at his own arrest, which is the comparison here.
why.Proverbs 10:9: 'He that perverteth his ways shall be known.' A general proverb, and the weakest of the three.

why.Matthew 5:44: 'Pray for them which despitefully use you.' The direct opposite of a prayer for vengeance.
why.Romans 12:19-21: 'Avenge not yourselves,' and 'overcome evil with good.' The Christian rule for wrongs left unpunished.
why.Luke 23:34: 'Father, forgive them.' Jesus praying for his own killers. The sharpest contrast in the case.

why.Romans 12:17-19: 'Recompense to no man evil for evil,' and 'live peaceably with all men.' The standard the raids fall under.
why.2 Corinthians 10:3-4: 'The weapons of our warfare are not carnal.' Set against a church wing that armed itself.

why.Deuteronomy 24:16: 'Every man shall be put to death for his own sin.' The rule against charging a child with a parent's fault.
why.Ezekiel 18:20: 'The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father.' The same principle, said even more plainly.
why.Mark 10:14: 'Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not.' Aimed at the bar on baptism.
why.Numbers 23:19: 'God is not a man, that he should… repent.' Cited about a revelation reversed four years later.

why.D&C 64:23: 'He that is tithed shall not be burned at his coming.' Canon, and the source of the fire language.
why.D&C 119:3-4: Sets the amount. 'One-tenth of all their interest annually,' and it is called a standing law for ever.
why.2 Corinthians 9:7: Give 'not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.' The verse against a required sum.
why.Matthew 23:23: Jesus on tithing mint and cummin while missing 'judgment, mercy, and faith.' Note that he does not abolish tithing.
why.Mark 12:41-44: The widow's two mites, praised for giving 'all her living.' Cuts both ways, since it commends costly giving.

why.Official Declaration 1: Where Woodruff's promise is printed. God 'will never permit' a president 'to lead you astray.' In their canon.
why.Deuteronomy 18:21-22: The fulfilment test. It covers predictions, not a prophet's wrong opinion, so use it carefully here.
why.Matthew 7:15-20: 'By their fruits ye shall know them.' A test of character and outcome, not of doctrinal detail.
why.1 Thessalonians 5:21: 'Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.' It makes checking a duty, not disloyalty.

why.Mark 9:42: 'Whosoever shall offend one of these little ones… a millstone.' Jesus's own weight on harming a child.
why.Luke 8:17: 'Nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest.' Aimed at a system that kept the report inside.
why.James 1:27: 'Pure religion' is to visit 'the fatherless and widows in their affliction.' Care for the weak as the test.

why.Deuteronomy 18:21-22: The test. A word given in the LORD's name that does not come to pass was not from him.
why.Proverbs 12:22: 'Lying lips are abomination to the LORD.' A weak fit here, since fraud was never established.
why.Jeremiah 23:21: 'I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran.' The charge of speaking without being sent.

why.Jacob 2:24-30: Their own book calls many wives 'abominable,' with the one exception clause. It frames the whole question.
why.D&C Official Declaration 1: The 1890 Manifesto itself, in their canon. Read the wording and see how narrow the promise is.
why.Proverbs 12:22: 'Lying lips are abomination to the LORD.' The measure applied to fifteen years of public denials.
why.Matthew 5:33-37: 'Let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.' Against careful wording meant to mislead.
why.Ephesians 4:25: 'Speak every man truth with his neighbour.' The plain rule for what leaders told members.
why.Numbers 30:2: A man who swears an oath 'shall not break his word.' Set beside the sworn Smoot testimony.

why.Abraham 1:12-15: The story the picture is said to show. Priests laying 'violence upon me' on an altar.
why.Book of Abraham, Facsimile 1 Explanation: Smith's own printed labels for each figure. That is the claim being tested.
why.Deuteronomy 18:21-22: The test for a claim made in God's name. Here it lands on a translation, not a prediction.
why.1 Thessalonians 5:21: 'Prove all things.' The warrant for checking a translation claim at all.

why.Abraham 3:2-4, 9: The Kolob text. Figure 1 is said to show it, so the two stand or fall together.
why.Book of Abraham, Facsimile 2 Explanation: Smith's own labels, including figure 7 as 'God sitting upon his throne.' The checkable part.
why.Deuteronomy 18:21-22: The test applied here. A named, specific claim made in God's name, which can be checked.
why.1 Thessalonians 5:21: 'Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.' Why checking is the faithful thing to do.

why.Book of Abraham, Facsimile 3 Explanation: The labels, including 'whose name is given in the characters above his head.' That is the testable part.
why.Deuteronomy 18:21-22: The test. Here it lands on a translation that can be checked against captions we can read.
why.Proverbs 12:22: 'Lying lips are abomination to the LORD.' A poor fit. This is about accuracy, not about intent to deceive.
why.1 Thessalonians 5:21: 'Prove all things.' The captions are printed in the book, so anyone can check them.

why.D&C 27:11: Their own canon calls Adam 'Michael… the ancient of days.' An archangel, not God.
why.D&C 107:53-55: God appears to Adam and the elders, who call Adam 'Michael, the prince, the archangel.' Both are present.
why.Genesis 2:7: Adam 'formed… of the dust of the ground.' A creature, made by God.
why.Hosea 11:9: 'I am God, and not man.' Short, and it lands straight on the claim.
why.Isaiah 43:10: 'Before me there was no God formed.' No room for a God who used to be Adam.
why.1 Corinthians 15:45: 'The first man Adam was made a living soul.' Made, and called the first man, not God.

why.D&C 13: The Aaronic priesthood text, given as John the Baptist's words. It first appears in print years after 1829.
why.D&C 27:5-13: The verses naming the angels. Compare them with Book of Commandments 28 and watch the passage grow.
why.Joseph Smith—History 1:68-72: The official account of the ordination, written up later. It is the version members learn.
why.Hebrews 7:23-24: Christ 'hath an unchangeable priesthood.' Used against the need for a restored line of authority.
why.1 Peter 2:9: Believers as 'a royal priesthood.' The New Testament gives that title to the whole church.
why.Deuteronomy 4:2: 'Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you.' Aimed at the 1835 additions.

why.D&C 5:4: The revised wording: 'no other gift until it is finished.' The 1833 printing had no such limit.
why.D&C 8:6-9: 'The gift of Aaron.' In 1833 the same gift was described as working with a rod.
why.D&C 27:5-13: The passage that grew from a short 1830 revelation into eighteen verses naming the angels.
why.Deuteronomy 4:2: 'Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it.'
why.Proverbs 30:5-6: 'Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee.' The second half of the same rule.

why.Abraham 1:1-3: The published English text. The Kirtland papers line it up against single Egyptian characters, one to a paragraph.
why.Deuteronomy 18:21-22: The fulfilment test, applied here to a translation claim made in God's name.
why.Jeremiah 23:16: Prophets who 'speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the LORD.' Heavy wording; use it with care.

why.Deuteronomy 18:21-22: The only reference here, and the test being applied. A vision claim about a real skeleton, which can be checked.

why.D&C 28:8: A mission 'unto the Lamanites' in New York state. Their canon places Lamanite peoples in North America.
why.D&C 32:2: The same mission, into 'the wilderness among the Lamanites.' A second case in their canon.
why.Mormon 6:6: The hill Cumorah of the last battle. For a century this was the New York hill, taught as doctrine.
why.Luke 3:1: Luke dates his account by named rulers and provinces. The Bible invites this kind of checking.
why.Acts 26:26: Paul says 'this thing was not done in a corner.' The Christian claim is meant to be placed on a map.

why.D&C 132:52-55: The threat in canon. Emma must accept, or 'she shall be destroyed,' with blessings promised to Joseph either way.
why.D&C 132:63-65: Widens it to any wife who refuses, and releases the husband from 'the law of Sarah.'
why.Jacob 2:24: Their own book calls many wives 'abominable.' That is what the angel account has to overturn.
why.Galatians 1:8: 'Though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel… let him be accursed.' Aimed at an angel's command.
why.2 Corinthians 11:14: 'Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.' Why an angel does not settle a question by itself.
why.Matthew 7:15-20: 'By their fruits ye shall know them.' This case is about character, so this is the right test.
why.Jeremiah 23:14: Prophets who 'commit adultery, and walk in lies.' Very heavy. It will land as an accusation, so weigh it first.

why.D&C 128:15-18: The doctrine. The dead 'cannot be made perfect' without us, and the work is 'essential to our salvation.'
why.Alma 34:32-35: Their own book says there is no labour after this life. That sits badly with work done for the dead.
why.1 Corinthians 15:29: 'Baptized for the dead.' The one verse the whole practice rests on, and Paul mentions it without commanding it.
why.Hebrews 9:27: 'Appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.' No window afterwards.
why.Luke 16:26: The 'great gulf fixed' between the dead and the living. Nothing passes across it.

why.D&C 134:9: Their own canon. 'We do not believe it just to mingle religious influence with civil government.'
why.Matthew 22:21: 'Render… unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's.' The usual verse for keeping the two apart.
why.John 18:36: 'My kingdom is not of this world.' Note that many Christians campaign too, so this cuts both ways.

why.D&C 119:3-4: The tithing law. It sets the duty, and says nothing about how the funds may be invested.
why.2 Corinthians 8:20-21: 'Providing for honest things… in the sight of men.' A standard for handling money, not proof of fraud.

why.2 Nephi 9:34: 'Wo unto the liar.' Their own scripture, which Dunn's published confession runs straight into.
why.Ephesians 4:25: 'Speak every man truth with his neighbour.' The plain standard for a preacher's stories.
why.Proverbs 12:22: 'Lying lips are abomination to the LORD.' Short, and already conceded by his apology.
why.Romans 3:7-8: Paul rejects doing evil 'that good may come.' That was Dunn's own first defence of the stories.

why.D&C 46:23-27: Their canon lists 'the discerning of spirits' among the gifts, given so the church is not deceived.
why.1 John 4:1: 'Try the spirits.' The duty of testing, which is what nobody did with Hofmann.
why.1 Corinthians 12:10: Paul's list of gifts, including 'discerning of spirits.' The New Testament source of the claim.

why.Moroni 10:4-5: The promise the whole missionary system rests on. Ask, and 'he will manifest the truth of it unto you.'
why.D&C 9:8-9: Where the feeling is defined. 'Your bosom shall burn within you,' against 'a stupor of thought.'
why.Alma 32:27-28: The seed experiment. The test is whether it 'beginneth to be delicious to me.' A feeling again.
why.Deuteronomy 13:1-3: The key verse. Reject a prophet whose doctrine is false, even when his sign comes true.
why.1 John 4:1: 'Believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God.' Testing is commanded.
why.Isaiah 8:20: 'To the law and to the testimony.' Written revelation as the measure of any new claim.
why.Acts 17:11: The Bereans 'searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.' Praised for checking Paul.
why.Jeremiah 17:9: 'The heart is deceitful above all things.' Why a feeling is not a safe instrument on its own.

why.Alma 36:1-30: The showpiece chapter. Read it and watch the shape turn on 'born of God' at the centre.
why.Genesis 9:6: A short biblical chiasm — blood, man, man, blood. It shows the form is real and old.
why.Amos 5:4-6: A longer example from the Bible. Nobody can say the form was invented to serve this argument.

why.1 Nephi 16:34: The verse. 'The place which was called Nahom' was already named, which is what makes it testable.
why.1 Nephi 17:1: The turn 'nearly eastward.' That is the second half of the match with the Yemen altars.
why.Proverbs 18:17: 'He that is first in his own cause seemeth just.' The rule for hearing both sides on a strong claim.

why.D&C 28:2-7: Only Joseph may 'receive commandments and revelations' for the church. That rule is what made 1844 a crisis.
why.D&C 43:3-4: Nobody else gets the gift except through him, and he may 'appoint another in his stead.' No appointment was produced.
why.3 Nephi 11:29: 'He that hath the spirit of contention is not of me.' Set against a movement that split four ways.
why.1 Corinthians 14:33: 'God is not the author of confusion.' The verse behind the whole argument from the split.
why.Matthew 7:15-20: 'By their fruits ye shall know them.' Applied here to what the succession actually produced.
why.Deuteronomy 18:21-22: The prophet test. It fits loosely, since this is about succession, not a failed prediction.

why.D&C 131:5: 'The more sure word of prophecy' — a man 'knowing that he is sealed up unto eternal life.' The rite's basis.
why.D&C 132:49: 'I seal upon you your exaltation, and prepare a throne for you.' The language the ordinance draws on.
why.2 Peter 1:10: 'Make your calling and election sure.' The phrase the rite borrows, from a public letter to all readers.
why.1 John 5:13: John writes 'that ye may know that ye have eternal life.' That is offered openly, to every believer.
why.Romans 8:16: 'The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit.' The witness comes straight to you, not by invitation.
why.Ephesians 2:8-9: 'By grace are ye saved through faith.' There is no tier of ordinances above that.

why.1 Nephi 13:28: The premise. 'Plain and precious things taken away from the book,' which is why a corrected Bible was needed.
why.D&C 45:60-61: The command to begin. 'I give unto you that ye may now translate it.'
why.D&C 73:3-4: The order to keep going 'until it be finished.' The work was commanded, not optional.
why.D&C 124:89: The command to 'publish the new translation.' It was never obeyed, which their own scholars grant.
why.Articles of Faith 1:8: The Bible is God's word 'as far as it is translated correctly.' That is why a revision was wanted.
why.Deuteronomy 4:2: 'Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you.' Aimed at some 3,400 changed verses.
why.Proverbs 30:5-6: 'Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee.' The same rule, put in Proverbs.
why.Isaiah 40:8: 'The word of our God shall stand for ever.' Against a Bible said to need wholesale repair.
why.1 Peter 1:24-25: Peter applies that promise to the gospel that was preached. The New Testament half of the same point.

why.Lectures on Faith 5 (1835 D&C: the Fathe: The lecture at issue. It calls the Father 'a personage of spirit,' which later teaching could not keep.
why.D&C 130:22: The later doctrine. The Father 'has a body of flesh and bones.' That is why Lecture 5 had to go.
why.1835 D&C title page and preface: The 1835 volume itself. It shows the Lectures printed as the 'Doctrine' half of the book.
why.Jude 3: 'The faith which was once delivered unto the saints.' Set against a canon edited by committee.
why.Isaiah 40:8: 'The word of our God shall stand for ever.' Against scripture that can be voted back out.
why.Malachi 3:6: 'I am the LORD, I change not.' Cited because the doctrine of God changed, and the canon followed.

why.D&C 57:1-3: The naming of the spot. Independence is 'the center place,' and the lot is 'not far from the courthouse.'
why.D&C 84:3-5: The temple promised on that lot. Lead with the ownership point, not the dating, which belongs elsewhere.
why.D&C 97:19: 'Zion cannot fall, neither be moved out of her place.' The confidence attached to the site.
why.Deuteronomy 18:22: The test. A word spoken in the LORD's name that does not come to pass was not his.

why.D&C 103:15-20: The promise. Zion redeemed 'by power,' under a man 'like as Moses,' with a stretched-out arm.
why.D&C 105:9-13: The walk-back, four months later. Wait 'a little season,' and the failure is put down to transgression.
why.D&C 101:17-18: 'Zion shall not be moved out of her place.' The earlier assurance the other two sit between.
why.Deuteronomy 18:21-22: The test. You need no outside source here, since promise and retraction are both in their canon.
why.Ezekiel 13:6-7: Prophets who 'made others to hope' with a word the LORD never spoke. Heavy. Say it gently or not at all.

why.D&C 85:7-8: The verse. God will send 'one mighty and strong… to set in order the house of God.' Still unfulfilled.
why.Deuteronomy 18:20-22: The prophet test, applied here to the claimants this verse produced.
why.Matthew 24:24: 'False Christs, and false prophets.' It fits the splinter leaders who claimed the title.

why.D&C 130:22: The canon behind the couplet. The Father 'has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's.'
why.King Follett discourse (Teachings of the: Where Joseph Smith taught that God was once a man. The couplet's source in his own preaching.
why.Psalm 90:2: 'From everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.' No earlier stage in which he was something else.
why.Isaiah 43:10: 'Before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.' It answers both halves of the couplet.
why.Numbers 23:19: 'God is not a man.' The shortest reply to the first half.
why.Malachi 3:6: 'I am the LORD, I change not.' A God who rose from manhood has changed a great deal.

why.2 Nephi 2:22: Without the Fall, all things 'must have remained forever, and had no end.' So no death before it.
why.Alma 12:23-24: 'There would have been no death' but for the Fall. The same commitment, stated again.
why.Moses 3:7: Adam as 'the first flesh upon the earth.' That leaves no room for earlier living things.
why.D&C 77:6-7: The earth's 'temporal existence' given as seven thousand years. A number the church no longer defends.
why.Genesis 1:26-27: 'God created man in his own image.' The point the 1909 statement was really defending.
why.Romans 5:12: 'By one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin.' Why death before Adam is a problem.

why.D&C 115:4: The verse Nelson cited. 'Thus shall my church be called… The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.'
why.3 Nephi 27:7-8: Jesus on calling a church by his name. Their strongest support here, and a fair one.
why.Acts 11:26: 'The disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.' A nickname given from outside, and it stuck.
why.1 Corinthians 1:12-13: 'I am of Paul; and I of Apollos.' Paul's worry about names is about faction, not branding.

why.Hymn 27, 'Praise to the Man': The hymn people point at. Read the words: high praise of a founder, not worship of him.
why.D&C 135:3: Says Smith did more 'save Jesus only' for salvation than any man. Note that phrase. It ranks him below Christ.
why.Exodus 20:3-5: 'Thou shalt have no other gods before me.' It does not apply, because nobody here is being worshipped.
why.Acts 10:25-26: Peter refuses worship: 'I myself also am a man.' A good principle, aimed at the wrong target.

why.D&C 89 (Word of Wisdom, the supposed iro: The only reference here. The joke needs a caffeine ban, and D&C 89 never mentions caffeine.

why.1 Peter 3:15-16: Answer 'with meekness and fear.' The verse that rules this line of attack out.
why.Colossians 4:6: 'Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt.' How to raise the real question instead.

why.D&C 132: The revelation on plural marriage. It is the real substance, and it needs no inflated wife count.

why.D&C 89:9 ('hot drinks are not for the bo: The verse the rumour hangs on. It says 'hot drinks,' and never mentions caffeine at all.
why.Mark 7:18-19: Jesus on what enters a man. It bears on the real question, which is worthiness rules, not fizzy drinks.
why.Colossians 2:20-23: 'Touch not; taste not; handle not.' Aim it at the worthiness bar, and state that bar correctly.

why.D&C 132:19-20: Use these words, not 'own planet.' 'Then shall they be gods, because they have all power.'
why.Moses 1:33: 'Worlds without number have I created.' Where the cosmic language actually comes from.
why.Isaiah 43:10: 'Before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.' Set it beside D&C 132:20.
why.Isaiah 44:6-8: 'Is there a God beside me? yea, there is no God.' The same denial, from God's own mouth.
